workout.session_type: BACK REHAB + ACTIVE RECOVERY (no spinal loading)
workout.warmup: 12-15 min incline walk, EASY - 3.0-3.3 mph at 4-6%. This is not a conditioning effort, it is blood flow to an irritated erector. Then Cat-Cow x 10 slow, and 90/90 hip switches x 10/side.
workout.coach_note: This is a treatment session, not a training session, and I want you to read it that way. Friday you tweaked the lower right side of your back hoisting a 50 lb dumbbell to your knee - the SETUP, not the press. Today is day four and it is still achy. You have trained three of the last four days around it: light RDLs Sunday, machines and reps-in-reserve today. All of that was the right call and I want that on the record. But your rotation puts a lower day here, and squats or hinges on a four-day-old erector strain is how two weeks becomes two months. So we spend one day paying it off. Nothing today loads your spine: no bar on your back, no hinge, no dumbbell lifted off the floor. Every DB you touch comes off a rack at hip height or higher - that is the exact mechanism that hurt you, and it is a setup habit worth fixing permanently. The Big 3 below (curl-up, side plank, bird dog) is the actual evidence-based protocol for a lumbar strain, not filler I padded the session with. Do it deliberately. If everything is quiet tomorrow you get a modified lower day Wednesday - leg press, extension, curl, all back-supported, still no loaded hinge. Your leg curl also earned 80 lb from that 12/12/12 on Aug 16, and it will be waiting for you when the hinge comes back. STOP RULE for today: anything sharp, anything that catches, you are done. Walk and go home.
workout.finisher: 10 min easy walk, flat or light incline. Total session should run 40-50 min.

exercises.name: McGill Big 3 - Modified Curl-Up
exercises.detail: 3 sets x 10 sec holds per side (hands under low back, one knee bent)
exercises.note: Hands palm-down under your lower back, one knee bent and one leg straight. Lift head and shoulders only an inch or two - this is a brace, not a crunch. Hold 10 seconds, breathe through it, down. Switch which knee is bent between sets. No chin tuck to the chest, no pulling on your neck. This one is deliberately unglamorous and it is the most useful thing you will do today.

exercises.name: McGill Big 3 - Side Plank
exercises.detail: 3 x 30 sec/side (from the knees if the full version pulls on the right side)
exercises.note: You have been holding 45 sec so this is a step DOWN on purpose. Hips stacked, body in one line, ribs down. Side planks load the obliques and quadratus lumborum without compressing the spine, which is exactly what an irritated erector wants. Start on your LEFT side (good side) so you know what normal feels like before you test the right.

exercises.name: McGill Big 3 - Bird Dog
exercises.detail: 3 x 8/side, 3 sec hold at the top
exercises.note: Opposite arm and leg, reach long rather than high - hand and heel push away from each other. Hips stay square, no rotation, no arching. Three-second pause at full extension. If your right side complains, shorten the reach rather than skipping the rep.

exercises.name: Supine Glute Bridge -> Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.detail: 2 x 15 double-leg, then 2 x 10/leg single-leg. Bodyweight only.
exercises.note: Zero spinal load, and it keeps your glutes firing while the hinge is benched. Ribs DOWN, squeeze at the top, do not arch your low back to get higher - that is the mistake that makes a bridge feel like a back exercise. For the single-leg version, hug the non-working knee loosely to your chest.

exercises.name: Banded Clamshell + Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.detail: 2 rounds: Clamshell x 15/side, Hip Abduction x 15/side
exercises.note: Glute medius work. Weak hip abductors make the lumbar spine do stabilizing work it should not be doing, which is relevant to a one-sided strain like yours. Light band or no band. Pelvis stays still - if you are rolling backward to get range, you are cheating it.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl - LIGHT
exercises.note: Deliberately 20 lb below your working weight. Back fully supported, no spinal compression, and it moves blood through the hamstrings, which pull on the pelvis and influence how your low back feels. This is circulation work, not a set you push. If the machine seat makes you round your lower back to get in position, skip it.

exercises.name: Leg Extension - LIGHT
exercises.note: Same logic - supported, easy, quad blood flow. Controlled tempo both directions, no slamming the stack. Skip if you are already at 50 minutes.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch + Standing Hamstring Stretch
exercises.note: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch: tuck the pelvis under BEFORE you push forward, or you just extend your lumbar spine and feel nothing in the hip. Four and a half hours in a car two weeks ago and a lot of travel since means your hip flexors are short, and short hip flexors tilt the pelvis and load the erectors. This is upstream of the actual problem.
